newsitem.title: INDIA: Sri Lankan president meets Indian PM Deve Gowda.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan president meets Indian PM Deve Gowda.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Bandaranaike Kumaratunga, currently on a week-long private visit to India, met Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Sunday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency said.
"Deve Gowda and Kumaratunga are understood to have had informal discussions on various issues including Indo-Sri Lanka relations," PTI reported.
Kumaratunga's visit has assumed added significance following speculation that she would try and negotiate peace with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
Kumaratunga arrived in Delhi on Tuesday, two days after the LTTE released 16 captured Sinhalese fishermen as part of a Christmas truce, an LTTE source said.
LTTE sources had said that Kumaratunga's government had encouraged a peace initiative undertaken recently by an international humanitarian group but they gave no details.

India has been closely involved in Sri Lanka's turbulent ethnic crises, providing armed assistance to Colombo in fending off a hardline Sinhalese-led rebellion and later by sending in troops there in a failed attempt in 1987 to disarm the LTTE.
Kumaratunga last visited India for a South Asian summit in May last year.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The Sri Lanka government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the ethnic conflict. The LTTE claims the number is much higher.
